source.title: Not All Adapters Matter: Selective Adapter Freezing for Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Language Models
source.authors: Hyegang Son; Yonglak Son; Changhoon Kim; Young Geun Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether selective freezing during fine-tuning changes held-out task performance and reports loss-flatness measurements, using a different intervention and measures from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study compares SAFE with LoRA on held-out task metrics and reports loss-landscape and Hessian analyses. It does not test random-label memorization, interpolation-threshold widening, the listed optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Prior-work comparisons are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own selective adapter-freezing method and uses the flatness–generalization connection to interpret its results. It tests none of V1–V8. In particular, normalized random-direction loss plots and Hessian eigenvalues do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of train–test gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SAFE reduces memory, computation, and training time while maintaining comparable or sometimes better task performance. They attribute improvements to regularization and flatter loss landscapes. Their analyses do not establish V7's specific sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses adaptive early freezing of adapters during pretrained-model fine-tuning; it does not apply the original studies' interventions or measures of random-label memorization, width, optimizer or batch-size generalization gaps, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported held-out metrics vary by model, task, and metric: SAFE improves SQuAD F1, is comparable to LoRA on E2E metrics with small increases and decreases, and the GLUE average rises from 84.66 to 84.99. The loss-flatness analyses are reported for BERTbase on QNLI and SST-2.

fits_no_version.finding: SAFE raises average BERTlarge GLUE score from 84.66 to 84.99 and improves all four reported SQuAD F1 comparisons. GPT-2medium E2E scores decrease slightly across all five metrics; GPT-2large results are nearly equal, with small changes in both directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective adapter freezing can preserve or modestly improve held-out NLP performance relative to LoRA while reducing resource use.

fits_no_version.finding: SAFE produces qualitatively flatter BERTbase loss landscapes on QNLI and SST-2 and reduces reported Hessian eigenvalue magnitudes relative to LoRA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective adapter freezing can flatten the measured loss landscape and reduce local curvature during pretrained-transformer fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: For LLaMA-2 7B fine-tuned on LaMini, the authors report no WikiText-2 quality degradation while reducing memory from 66.35 GB to 34.20 GB; exact perplexity values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective adapter freezing can reduce LLaMA-2 7B fine-tuning memory while preserving reported WikiText-2 perplexity performance.

record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No train-test error gaps are reported. The loss landscape and Hessian results are qualitative in the supplied text, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. WikiText-2 perplexity values are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: Not all reported results are extracted. Table 1 task-specific GLUE metrics; further average resource measures; image-classification results in Table 5; compatibility results in Table 6; and adapter importance, CKA similarity, and memory-usage measurements in Figures 2–5 are omitted because they concern task-specific performance, resource use, or adapter representation rather than one of the listed claim versions. The paper's result descriptions mention similar freezing patterns in other tasks but provide figure-based detail not recorded here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error behavior when width increases beyond that needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers trained from scratch, including the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. AdamW is used without an optimizer comparison.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that alter the penalty.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on configuration, dataset size, or augmentation. LoRA dropout is fixed at 0.1.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8, not judgments that the reported method comparisons are unreadable. R1–R16 are method-performance results and should not serve as claim-test rows. No omitted result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and test performance alongside natural-label generalization.
Width sweep beyond interpolation threshold and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Adding or removing dropout and its interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measured against train-test gaps and compared with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: BERTbase
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss landscapes of LoRA and SAFE.
rows.value: SAFE yields a flatter loss landscape
rows.note: Qualitative result; text attributes flattening to SAFE. No train-test gap measurement.
rows.check: The qualitative flattening is reported, but the normalized random-direction visualization does not establish magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with train–test gaps required by V7.

rows.subject: BERTbase
rows.operation_detail: Compared top-5 Hessian eigenvalue spectrum for LoRA and SAFE.
rows.value: SAFE reduces the magnitude of Hessian eigenvalues
rows.note: The paper says the analysis is quantitative, but provides no numerical values in the supplied text.
rows.check: Reduced Hessian eigenvalue magnitudes are reported, but this is a different sharpness measure from V7 and no train–test-gap ranking is tested. Section 5.3 places this analysis alongside the BERTbase QNLI/SST-2 landscape comparison, rather than an entirely unspecified setting.
